text:
alex: RFC follow-up: prototype for drift detection using synthetic shadowing + KL-divergence on token distributions. Goal: detect subtle quality drift that degscore misses. Putting notes here and asking ops/telemetry for feedback.

maria: Interesting. How do you generate the synthetic shadowing set? We need it to be representative without leaking PII.

alex: We seed a small corpus per-endpoint: mix of user-anonized prompts + canonical probes derived from eval suites. We run ref vs quant and build per-token distribution histograms.

sam: KL is sensitive to zero bins; use smoothed histograms (additive smoothing) or JS divergence. Also need to pick binning: token-level vs logprob buckets.

jorge: Ops concern: running periodic ref runs is expensive. What's cadence? And how do we avoid on-path cost?

alex: Offline only. Cadence default: hourly for high-traffic endpoints, daily for low traffic. We sample <0.1% of traffic for production shadowing. Heavy lifting happens in batch jobs.

maria: Metric set proposal: js_divergence, deg_delta_mean, tail_snr, percent_tail_shift, and a synthetic_confidence (how well synthetic set matches prod distribution).

sam: For alerts: set multi-signal rule so KL spike alone won't Pager. e.g., js_divergence > X && deg_delta_mean > Y for > grace_period. Also add rate-limit so transient noise doesn't flip.

jorge: For remediation: propose 'rollback-safe mode' state that forces runtime to avoid low-bit profiles but keeps traffic flowing. Difference between rollback and drift_lock?

alex: Rollback-safe mode = automatic conservative action: pick first compatible profile that keeps same KV-format and has higher precision; if none, fall back to ref model but mark as grace_rebuild (may invalidate cache). Drift_lock is manual lock requiring review.

maria: Need clear API flags: auto_rollback_enabled (bool), rollback_max_cost_delta (float), rollback_reason_code (string). Also store provenance for the decision (js_divergence+prod-sample).

sam: Telemetry needs a histogram of js_divergence over time and a per-customer baseline. Also compute a z-score against baseline to reduce threshold tuning.

jorge: Can we estimate rollback cost before applying? If fallback invalidates cache, cost could be high. We should compute estimated_rebuild_ms and estimated_cost_tokens and only auto-rollback if under threshold.

alex: Good. Add profile metadata fields: synthetic_probe_id, baseline_js, auto_rollback_enabled, rollback_cost_est_ms, rollback_cost_tokens, compatible_profile_ids (prefer same-kv first).

maria: Privacy: ensure synthetic probes do not include user content. For endpoints with high privacy needs, only use canonical probes. Add probe_privacy_level to profile metadata.

sam: Also add a dry_run flag in runtime so we can log intended rollbacks for 48h before enabling auto-rollback. Useful for tuning.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created batch job `synthetic-shadow-batch` in staging; schedule hourly; sampling job and JS divergence calc.

jorge: Ops playbook for auto-rollback: 1) Verify js_divergence zscore > threshold AND deg_delta_mean > delta. 2) Check rollback_cost_ms < 200 and rollback_cost_tokens within budget. 3) If pass and auto_rollback_enabled -> apply safe-profile switch and notify owners. 4) If failed, mark for manual review and trigger incident channel.

alex: Add audit event with decision payload: {reason, signals, chosen_profile, estimated_cost, provenance}. We'll log to longterm retention for investigations.

maria: Owners: alex (drift logic), sam (telemetry), jorge (ops). I'll add dashboards for synthetic_confidence, js_divergence_z, rollback_attempts, rollback_success_rate.

sam: I'll wire canary: 0.5% traffic on staging then ramp. We'll run dry_run for 72h before flip.

jorge: One last thought: for long-running streams, some drift shows only after many tokens. Consider a trailing-window JS check (e.g., per-128-token windows). But beware compute cost. Maybe experimental.

alex: Noted. We'll add as experimental flag 'trailing_window_enabled' behind feature flag.

maria: Great. Alex, please drop an RFC appendix with: 1) probe generation rules, 2) JS divergence calc & smoothing, 3) profile metadata additions, 4) rollback-safe-mode state transitions and thresholds, 5) ops playbook and canary plan.

alex: Will do and ping this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
